clue.text: Those inside can get away in this

definitions.text: Those inside can get away in this

parts.words: Those inside can get away in this
parts.note: those inside are prisoners, and the thing they get away in is an escape from jail rather than a vehicle

explanation.surface: Something roomy that lets its passengers make a getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get away in this' suggests a car; the people 'inside' are convicts, and they get away in an escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison escape is the means by which inmates break out.

clue.text: Envious, having looked after historian

indicators.note: after places the word for looked behind the historian's name

parts.note: J. R. Green was a Victorian English historian
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: A jealous scholar who has been studying another historian's work.
explanation.walkthrough: J. R. Green wrote the popular Short History of the English People.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealousy is proverbially the green-eyed monster, so the compound is an idiom for covetous.

clue.text: Mix one up in order to make a sedative

indicators.note: in puts the mixed letters inside the letters for order

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

indicators.note: mix tells us to stir the letters of one and up together

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A pharmacist's instruction to prepare a tranquilliser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' is not a command but an honour: OM, the British Order of Merit.
explanation.definitionFit: The poppy drug is a narcotic once used to dull pain and induce sleep.

clue.text: City comedian in short dressing-gown

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England

indicators.note: in short tells us to cut the last letter off the comedian's surname

parts.note: George Robey was a famous British music-hall comedian

explanation.surface: A city-dwelling comic appears in an abbreviated house-coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' docks the final Y from ROBEY. George Robey was a hugely popular English music-hall comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A towelling robe worn after bathing is a kind of loose gown for lounging.

clue.text: Reappearance of celestial body — one featured by US poet

indicators.note: featured by means the numeral appears within the poet's name

parts.note: Ralph Waldo Emerson was an American poet and essayist
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An astronomer notes a planet's return, quoted in an American poem.
explanation.definitionFit: In astronomy the term names a star or moon coming back into view after an eclipse or occultation.

clue.text: King from sunset to sunrise is a lesser man

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
the hours between dusk and dawn are the night

explanation.surface: A monarch who is diminished in the dark hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' is a chess piece: this one ranks below the king.
explanation.definitionFit: On a chessboard the horse-shaped piece is a minor piece, of lower worth than the monarch.

clue.text: Bed the Sappers give father in the army

parts.note: a pad is slang for a bed or place to sleep
RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers

explanation.surface: Army engineers provide a bunk for the regimental priest.
explanation.definitionFit: The forces' chaplain is addressed as a clergyman, and 'father' is a title for a priest.

clue.text: One who puts out flags?

parts.note: flags here are flagstones, so the person laying them out is a paving worker, not someone hanging bunting

explanation.surface: Someone decorating the street for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Flags are paving stones, so this is a person who lays a pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: The worker sets paving slabs in place, laying out flagstones.

clue.text: River plank is target for missiles

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon
a board is a plank of wood

explanation.surface: A plank by the riverside is used for shooting practice.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dart is a river in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: In the pub game, darts are the thrown missiles and this round board is what they are aimed at.

clue.text: Requiem for example in the Cathedral

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation inside the cathedral's name

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A requiem mass, for instance, is performed in the minster.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely, in Cambridgeshire, is famous for its cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A mournful poem or song for the dead is a lament, as a requiem is.

clue.text: Letter vital to orthoepist learning pronunciation

indicators.note: vital to means forming part of the body of these words, so the answer sits within them

explanation.surface: A note that is essential for a student of correct speech.
explanation.walkthrough: An orthoepist studies correct pronunciation; the answer spans 'orthoEPIST LEarning'.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament's Pauline writings are formal letters, so the word names a written missive.

clue.text: Contrary way a poet works we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is spoken and heard as a single word

parts.note: a poet writes ..., and those two words run together make the sound

explanation.surface: A contrary poet's method, as we are told it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' tells us the two-word phrase 'in verse', how a poet writes, is said as one word; spelt as one word it means opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means opposite or reversed in order, which is what contrary means.

clue.text: Vicar baptizing has to get title right

parts.note: a title is a name

explanation.surface: A clergyman at a christening must get the child's label correct.
explanation.walkthrough: At a christening the vicar gives the child a name, so a baptizing vicar is one who names.
explanation.definitionFit: Christening a baby means giving it its first name, so the officiant is the one conferring it.

clue.text: One expected to learn part of Jaques soliloquy

definitions.meaning: a pupil is someone expected to study and learn
Jaques's 'All the world's a stage' speech in As You Like It lists the seven ages, one of them the whining pupil

explanation.walkthrough: Jaques, in Shakespeare's As You Like It, describes the seven ages of man, the second being the 'whining' pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy at school is a pupil, and Shakespeare's seven ages include the reluctant pupil creeping to lessons.

clue.text: Pine cut down — reserve for an annual

indicators.note: cut down means the last letter is lopped off the word for pine

parts.note: to pine is to yearn
to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: A felled pine tree is put aside for the gardener's yearly plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' trims YEARN to YEAR. 'Pine' looks like a tree with 'cut down' but is the verb, and 'annual' looks like a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a publication issued once a year, like a school's commemorative volume.

clue.text: Maori being without capital moves to become Australian

indicators.note: moves tells us the remaining letters shift into a new order
without capital means losing the opening capital letter of the word Maori

explanation.surface: A New Zealander who has lost his capital relocates to Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without capital' drops the M of Maori; 'moves' rearranges AORI plus BEING.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an original inhabitant of Australia, a native Australian.

clue.text: Perch in a tree?

definitions.meaning: the fish is a spiny-finned relative of the perch, so perch here is a fish
the American lime or linden tree is known as basswood

explanation.walkthrough: 'Perch' looks like a bird's resting place but is a fish; basswood is the American linden tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea fish is a close relative of the perch, and basswood is a North American linden tree.

clue.text: Academic subtle about choral arrangement

indicators.note: about means the word for subtle goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: sly means subtle or cunning

indicators.note: arrangement means the letters of choral are rearranged, as music is arranged

explanation.surface: A clever scholar works on a crafty choral setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subtle' gives the cunning sense, not delicate; 'about' signals the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic and the answer both describe learned, studious work.

clue.text: Note receipt is altered amounts to be broken down

parts.note: D is a musical note

indicators.note: is altered tells us the letters of receipt change their order

explanation.surface: A banknote's receipt has been changed, the sums are disintegrating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amounts to be' is a long link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worn out by age is dilapidated, as a broken-down old car is.

clue.text: Patball with the feet?

parts.note: patball is a gentle hand game of patting a ball; done with the feet the patting becomes rhythmic stepping

explanation.surface: A gentle ball game played with the feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Patball is a gentle game of patting a ball to and fro; 'pat' with the feet gives tapping steps.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of dancing uses metal-tipped shoes to beat rhythms on the floor.

clue.text: Opening for GP incorporating two rounds

indicators.note: incorporating means the doctor's abbreviation takes the rounds inside it

parts.note: a GP is a doctor, abbreviated Dr
each round is the letter O, so two rounds give O and O

explanation.surface: A doctor's surgery entrance takes in two patients' rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: A GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrance or way in is an opening.

clue.text: Girl given free hand in gallery

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name

indicators.note: free means the letters of hand are released into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl is given free rein in an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges HAND to NDAH.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofed open gallery along the outside of a house is a porch or veranda.

clue.text: The way to hold a revolutionary packet of shampoo

indicators.note: to hold means the street abbreviation encloses the other letters

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
Che Guevara was a Marxist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A guerrilla leader carries a small pouch of hair wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The way' reads as a manner of doing something, but it is a street; Che Guevara is the stock revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sealed sachet holds a single dose of liquid such as hair wash.

clue.text: Leafy feature of centre where Eve came from

parts.note: mid means middle or centre
in Genesis Eve was made from Adam's rib

explanation.surface: A garden scene linking the centre of Eden with Eve's origin.
explanation.definitionFit: The central vein running down a leaf is its main rib.

clue.text: Army officer exploited by author

parts.note: Conan Doyle wrote The Exploits of ... Gerard, so this officer had his exploits written up by an author

explanation.surface: A soldier taken advantage of by a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploited' refers to Conan Doyle's stories The Exploits of Brigadier Gerard.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank above colonel is a senior army officer, and Doyle's Gerard held it.

clue.text: Instrument to rule out for a March

parts.note: to ban is to rule out
Jo March is a heroine of Little Women

explanation.surface: A musical instrument to be banned from a marching band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like a month or parade but is the family surname in Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: The stringed instrument with a round drum body is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Almost succeed as a joiner

indicators.note: almost means the phrase falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: to do well is to succeed

explanation.surface: A carpenter who very nearly makes good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last L from DO WELL; a joiner is a carpenter, but here the thing that joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden peg fitted into holes in two pieces holds them together, so it joins them.

clue.text: Smoke from a boat

definitions.meaning: a puff of smoke, or a small cigar

explanation.walkthrough: The less familiar sense is a light outrigged rowing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A puff of smoke or small cigar is one sense, and a light sculling skiff is another.

clue.text: Not one to move therein

indicators.note: to move tells us the letters of therein shift around

explanation.surface: Nobody there is willing to relocate inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means not either of two, so not one of the pair.

clue.text: Gun girl in Puerto Rico carried by a donkey

indicators.note: in puts the girl's name inside the abbreviation

parts.note: Annie is the heroine of the musical Annie Get Your Gun

explanation.surface: A sharpshooting woman in the Caribbean rides a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gun girl' is Annie Oakley of the musical Annie Get Your Gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A basket slung over a pack animal's back is a load the animal carries.

clue.text: Past the start of the patent

parts.note: over means past, finished

indicators.note: start of means only the opening letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: An expired patent is past its beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patent' is the adjective meaning plain, not the inventor's licence.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent means plain to see, open and evident.

clue.text: Madame having a stroke?

definitions.meaning: a swimming stroke with both arms moving together

explanation.walkthrough: Puccini's opera is Madama Butterfly; there is also a swimming stroke of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's tragic heroine bears the insect's name, and so does a two-arm swimming stroke.
